instruction: I have a video file at ~/video.mp4. Please extract just the audio track and save it as 'audio.mp3' in the same directory.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened terminal, used ffprobe to inspect video streams, extracted embedded subtitles with ffmpeg to SRT format, and also created a subtitle-free video copy. Demonstrated strong CLI and ffmpeg proficiency.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, navigate directories, use ffprobe to inspect media streams, use ffmpeg for stream extraction and remuxing, verify output files with ls and head
metadata.task_rationale: Related ffmpeg task: extracting audio instead of subtitles, tests same toolchain with a different stream type
metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the audio track from a video using ffmpeg. Getter checks if audio.mp3 exists, is a valid audio file, and has meaningful content. Partial credit: 0.34 file exists + 0.33 valid audio + 0.33 has content.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks file existence at /home/user/audio.mp3 matching the instruction's target path
Getter uses ffprobe to validate the output is a genuine audio file, not just any file renamed to .mp3
Getter checks file has meaningful size (>1KB) to ensure non-trivial content was extracted
Metric provides sensible partial credit breakdown: 0.34 (exists) + 0.33 (valid audio) + 0.33 (has content)
No postconfig needed since this is a file-based task with no UI state dependency
Metric does not misuse the expected parameter (it simply doesn't use it, which is acceptable)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a check that the audio duration is similar to the source video duration, to verify the audio was actually extracted from the video rather than being an arbitrary audio file
The expected parameter with rules={'check': 'audio_mp3_extracted'} is unused by the metric - could be removed or the metric could reference it for documentation clarity
